title: Quick Start: Sewing Tools (4)
description:

By the end of this tutorial, you'll be well-equipped with the knowledge to drape and simulate your garment in 3D.

transcript: Welcome to the quick start tutorial on Sewing Tools. You can either select the sewing tool you want or undock the Sewing Tools tab. Select the segment tool and click on the first segment on the back panel. And then on the second segment where you want it to be sewn together. As you can see, the sewing relationship is displayed in the 2D window with the notch lines and in the 3D window with a number of segmented lines. At times it can get confusing to know where one pattern should be sewn to another pattern. Clicking in the 3D window on the area of the pattern you want sewn will reveal a blue, dot in the 2D window. This will show you where the patterns need to be sewn together. Because these are symmetrical patterns, when you sew one side, the other side is also sewn. Select the Free Sewing tool and click on the edge of the pocket where it should be sewn. Drag the mouse to the right of the pocket. Press to the end of the pocket and click again. Repeat this on the pocket outline to complete the sewing relationship. Sewing can also be done in the 3D window. Undock the Sewing Tools to see them clearly. Hover the mouse over the avatar icon and select Show Arrangement Points. This will reveal a bunch of blue dots all over the avatar's body. Select a pattern and click on a dot closest to where the pattern should be in 3D space. Do this for the remaining patterns. You can move the patterns to adjust them if they don't look quite right. For the pocket, I'm just moving it near to where it should be. Symmetrical patterns will move to the corresponding dot on the other side. Use the Segment Sewing tool in the 3D window to sew the sleeve. If you sew two pieces together and the sewing is complete, then you're done. If you sew two pieces together and the sewing direction is wrong, go into the 2D window. Select Edit Sewing. Right-click on this sewing relationship and select Reverse Sewing. Remember when sewing that you can sew either in the 3D window or in the 2D window. If you want to do this in the 3D window, you can do this in the 3D window. If you want to do this in the 3D window, you can do this in the 3D window. Once the sewing is finished, press the Simulation button and simulate the shirt. It should fall into place. As you can see, the pocket opens as it should. To remove the unnecessary internal pocket line from the right side of the shirt, To remove the unnecessary internal pocket line from the right side of the shirt, Right-click and remove Link Editing. Now using the Transform Pattern tool, you can delete the unnecessary internal lines. Although Segment Sewing and Free Sewing are the two main sewing tools you will use, I will show you now the M in Sewing Tools. Use the Shift-Z hotkey to display the segment lengths. This is useful to see how long pattern segment lengths are. Select the M in Free Sewing tool. Click on the first pattern. Drag to the end. Press Enter. Then select the next pattern. And then the next pattern. And select Enter to complete it. You can use the Check Sewing Length tool to display the length difference and the ratio difference. Here I will stitch one pattern piece to another pattern piece that is much longer. You can also hover over the sewing relationship to see the length difference displayed in red. The width of M size is equal to the measurement length of Segment Sewing fürs Segment Length for the print.
summary: ```# Quick Start: Sewing Tools (4) ## Overview Welcome to the quick start tutorial on Sewing Tools. In this session, you will learn how to utilize various sewing tools effectively within the software. ## Selecting and Using the Segment Tool You can either select the sewing tool you want or undock the Sewing Tools tab. 1. **Select the Segment Tool**: Click on the first segment on the back panel. 2. **Choose the Second Segment**: Click on the second segment where you want it to be sewn together. As you can see, the sewing relationship is displayed in the 2D window with the notch lines and in the 3D window with a number of segmented lines. ## Understanding Sewing Relationships At times, it can get confusing to know where one pattern should be sewn to another pattern. Clicking in the 3D window on the area of the pattern you want sewn will reveal a blue dot in the 2D window. This will show you where the patterns need to be sewn together. Because these are symmetrical patterns, when you sew one side, the other side is also sewn. ## Using the Free Sewing Tool 1. **Select the Free Sewing Tool**: Click on the edge of the pocket where it should be sewn. 2. **Drag the Mouse**: Move to the right of the pocket. 3. **Click Again**: Press to the end of the pocket and click again. Repeat this on the pocket outline to complete the sewing relationship. ## Sewing in the 3D Window Sewing can also be done in the 3D window. Undock the Sewing Tools to see them clearly. 1. **Show Arrangement Points**: Hover the mouse over the avatar icon and select Show Arrangement Points. This will reveal a bunch of blue dots all over the avatar's body. 2. **Select a Pattern**: Click on a dot closest to where the pattern should be in 3D space. Do this for the remaining patterns. 3. **Adjust Patterns**: You can move the patterns to adjust them if they don't look quite right. For the pocket, move it near to where it should be. Symmetrical patterns will move to the corresponding dot on the other side. ## Segment Sewing Tool Use the Segment Sewing tool in the 3D window to sew the sleeve. If you sew two pieces together and the sewing is complete, then you're done. If you sew two pieces together and the sewing direction is wrong: 1. **Edit Sewing**: Go into the 2D window. 2. **Reverse Sewing**: Right-click on this sewing relationship and select Reverse Sewing. ## Sewing in 2D or 3D Remember, when sewing, you can sew either in the 3D window or in the 2D window. ## Simulation of the Finished Product Once the sewing is finished, press the Simulation button and simulate the shirt. It should fall into place. As you can see, the pocket opens as it should. ## Removing Unnecessary Lines To remove the unnecessary internal pocket line from the right side of the shirt: 1. **Link Editing**: Right-click and remove Link Editing. 2. **Transform Pattern Tool**: Now using the Transform Pattern tool, you can delete the unnecessary internal lines. ## Additional Sewing Tools Although Segment Sewing and Free Sewing are the two main sewing tools you will use, I will show you now the M in Sewing Tools. 1. **Display Segment Lengths**: Use the Shift-Z hotkey to display the segment lengths. This is useful to see how long pattern segment lengths are. 2. **Using the M in Free Sewing Tool**: - Click on the first pattern. - Drag to the end and press Enter. - Select the next pattern and then the next pattern. - Press Enter to complete it. 3. **Check Sewing Length Tool**: You can use the Check Sewing Length tool to display the length difference and the ratio difference. Here, I will stitch one pattern piece to another pattern piece that is much longer. You can also hover over the sewing relationship to see the length difference displayed in red. The width of M size is equal to the measurement length of Segment Sewing for the segment length for the print. ```
